title: fix(cli): run an app's onEnable and its handlers from one module evaluation
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbTGhxJSYAmQXU7efVdNqrpw)_

Fixes #34179

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none (boot composition; no authorable key changes; the dev confirms against the diff)

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：从编译产物启动时，应用的 job/hook/action 处理函数改为和 `onEnable` 取自同一次加载的配置模块，不再一部分取自产物里打包的 runtime 模块（那是同一份源码的第二次求值）。
- 为什么改：`onEnable` 在模块级保存的状态（例如 duly 的数据引擎）在 job 里读不到，`os dev` 下 job 每次都报 "no data engine"；实测非 host 配置的 `os start` 生产启动也一样。
- 风险与回滚：只影响从产物启动且配置带 `onEnable` 的启动；元数据仍取自产物。产物里有、源码里已没有的处理函数保持原样，并打印一次警告。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/cli/src/utils/graft-runtime-hooks.ts`（`graftAuthoredRuntimeMembers` 的改指向逻辑），然后是 `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` 的两处调用和警告文案。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit src/utils/graft-runtime-hooks.test.ts`，预期 21 个用例全绿，其中 "a job handler and a hook see the state onEnable bound" 通过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

A boot that serves the compiled artifact gets the app's callables from the artifact's runtime module (`dist/objectstack-runtime.*.mjs`). `loadArtifactBundle` imports that module and `mergeRuntimeModule` merges its `functions`. The module is an esbuild bundle of the same config source, so it is a second evaluation of it, with its own module state. serve then grafted the loaded config module's `onEnable` beside those callables. So `onEnable` and the handlers ran from two evaluations, and state that `onEnable` binds at module scope never reached a handler.

`graftAuthoredRuntimeMembers` (now async, still the one graft both serve routes call) closes the split. The re-point runs only when the target bundle has a `runtimeModule` and runs the config module's `onEnable`. In that case every callable the runtime module supplied is replaced, ref for ref, with the config module's own callable. The ref map is `lowerCallables(normalizeStackInput(config)).functions`, the same reading `os compile` writes the runtime module from. Each entry keeps its declaration (`effect`, and so on), and no entry without a callable gains one. The lowering is loaded lazily, so a boot without the split does not load the TypeScript parser.

- **Doors fixed:** `os dev` on a host config (the `devArtifactDoor` wrap) and on a non-host config, and `os start` / `os serve` on a non-host config (the standalone stack plus the `hasAppPluginAlready` graft). The production path was measured double-evaluating too.
- **Doors unchanged:** a boot from an artifact alone (no config module, so no `onEnable` at all), and host `os start` (it already wraps the module, one evaluation).
- **Stale artifact:** if the artifact names a ref the config no longer serves (for example `os dev --no-compile` over an older build), that callable stays on the runtime module. The boot then warns once and names it.

Files:
- `packages/cli/src/utils/graft-runtime-hooks.ts`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` (both call sites, the warning, the #31761 docblock)
- `packages/cli/src/utils/graft-runtime-hooks.test.ts` (pins; existing cases now `await`)
- `packages/cli/test/normalized-call-sites.test.ts` (one `top-level` row for the deliberate `bundle.functions` read, granted by the area)
- `.changeset/34179-dev-one-module-evaluation.md` (patch)

## Tests

The new pin composes the boot from the real producer to the real reader, in the cli unit tier. It runs an in-process `os compile` on a fixture whose `onEnable` binds a module-scope engine. A `functions` entry (the shape a job `handler` names) and a hook read that engine. The pin loads the artifact with the runtime's own `loadArtifactBundle`, loads the config with serve's `bundleConfigModule`, and wraps it in a real `AppPlugin`. It then reads handlers through `collectBundleFunctions`, the map job and string-named hook handlers resolve against. It asserts that both handlers see the engine. Further cases cover a stale ref (reported, left alone), the array form, a bundle with no runtime module, and a bundle whose own `onEnable` won (both untouched).

## Acceptance notes

- **Artifact-only boot:** it runs no `onEnable` because the runtime module exports only `functions`. This is a single evaluation and the documented behaviour (the job context hands `ql` for that reason), so it is not this defect.
- **`--no-compile` with matching refs:** handlers now run the edited source's code beside the artifact's metadata. That is the rule the #31761 docblock states: the module contributes the members a JSON artifact cannot carry. `onEnable` already came from the module there.

## Verification

Head e367244114 (`origin/main` merged). Session `session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5`.

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` mutated the re-point line (anchor x1 to x0; blob 4ae519b830d2 to 250315e758f2), then ran the pin file:

```
     × a job handler and a hook see the state onEnable bound
     × re-points the refs the module serves and reports the ones it does not (an artifact older than its source)
     × re-points the array form too, and never gives an entry without a callable one
```

<details><summary>Real boots: a 1 s interval job writes the module state onEnable set</summary>

Built `bin/run.js`, `OS_AUTOMATION_SCHEDULED_WORK_ENABLED=true`. The "main" column is this build with the re-point line removed from `dist/` (restored by sha256 afterwards). It is the same composition as `main`, not a separate build.

| door | main | this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|
| host config, `os dev` | `unset` | `bound` |
| host config, `os start` | `bound` | `bound` |
| non-host config, `os dev` | `unset` | `bound` |
| non-host config, `os start` | `unset` | `bound` |
| artifact only, `os start` | `unset` (no onEnable runs) | `unset` (unchanged) |

Host `os dev --no-compile` with refs matching: `bound`. With the job's function renamed in source after compiling: `unset`, plus this warning:

```
⚠ 1 handler of the compiled artifact (mm_job) has no counterpart in objectstack.config.ts as this boot evaluated it, so it runs from ./objectstack-runtime.433af1218610613d.mjs, a second evaluation of
    the same source: module state its onEnable sets is not visible there. Recompile (os compile) so the
    artifact matches the config.
```
</details>
